name: Venizelism
summary: Venizelism is the Greek liberal-nationalist current built around Eleftherios Venizelos and his Liberal Party. It combined state modernization, rule of law, moderate capitalism with protectionism and some social legislation, a crowned-democracy or republican constitutional preference, pro-Entente and pro-Western alignment, and the irredentist Megali Idea of uniting Greek-populated lands. It opposed both the palace-centred conservative establishment and Bolshevism.
scope: The mainstream Venizelism of 1910-1936: Venizelos's Liberal Party governments (1910-14, 1917-20, 1924, 1928-32), the 1911 constitutional revision, the National Schism and the Paris Peace Conference claims, with the later Centrist heirs excluded. Many answers on modern social and technological questions are low-confidence inferences from liberal-nationalist principles.

sources.usedFor: Rights, expropriation for landless farmers, free compulsory education, civil-service tenure, katharevousa as official language.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a Venizelist program item; a liberal-modernizing state with a social-democratic wing would accept public health provision, inferred from the mixed-economy label.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: No minimum wage existed in the era; the 1910-14 labour laws regulated hours and child labour but adherents later ranged from liberal to social democratic.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Venizelism backed moderate capitalism with open markets but required government approval and adopted strict protectionism, so it was neither laissez-faire nor statist.

public-ownership.rationale: The movement favoured early moderate capitalism and state planning by engineers rather than nationalization; inferred from that mixed record.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The 1911 constitution stressed equality in tax burdens but no program of soaking the rich is documented.

unions-good.rationale: The 1910-14 Liberal governments legalized labour organizations while the 1929 Idionymon curbed communist agitation, indicating a moderate pro-union stance.

property-fundamental.rationale: The 1911 revision kept property rights judicially protected even while allowing expropriation for landless farmers, so property is protected but not absolute.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Government approval of markets implies oversight, but no corporate regulation agenda is documented; inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: A modernizing state with social-democratic strands would not call for cutting welfare; inferred, not documented.

worker-ownership.rationale: Venizelism's moderate capitalism and anti-Bolshevism make collective worker ownership foreign to it.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; the Idionymon law shows willingness to police subversion but no view on surveillance as such.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Anachronistic; a bourgeois liberal-nationalist of the 1910s would be conservative on drugs.

strong-leader.rationale: Venizelos led by electoral mandate and also backed Plastiras-type officers; adherents were split between the leader-centred charisma and constitutional legalism.

state-harmful.rationale: The movement built a modern state with rule of law and technical planning; the idea of a harmful state is the opposite.

empower-police-military.rationale: Venizelos reformed and reinforced the army and navy with French and British missions and modernized administration.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Anachronistic; a liberal bourgeois movement of the period was likely conventional on morals.

decide-locally.rationale: Venizelism pursued centralizing modernization and a unified nation-state, inferred.

rehabilitation.rationale: No penal view documented; the 1911 text improved judicial independence only.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred from the conventional social values of an Orthodox Greek liberal party; not documented.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic; a committed adherent in the historical movement would reject it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from conventional social values.

more-religion-public.rationale: The movement is described as secularist and Venizelos avoided religious references in the Cretan constitution so that all residents felt represented.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not applicable to the movement's context.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Liberal-based nationalism and the Megali Idea of uniting Hellenic lands imply valuing Greek culture and tradition.

gradual-change.rationale: Venizelos favored limited constitutional revision, yet led the Goudi-era reforms and a Thessaloniki rebellion in 1916.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's own population policy involved resettling refugees.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Anachronistic; Venizelos relied on the Peace Conference and Allied great powers rather than a world body.

free-trade.rationale: A strict protectionism was adopted to promote Greece's rudimentary industry.

nation-first.rationale: Venizelism put the national cause of unification above neutrality, though it pursued it through alliance with the Entente.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Venizelos invoked protection of Greek populations and refugees, but this is not a general doctrine.

open-borders.rationale: A nation-state irredentist movement favouring one state per predominantly ethnic territory rejects open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: A modernizing economic-development movement would reject degrowth; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate policy is anachronistic for a 1910s-30s movement, and none of the sources record any position; left neutral at low confidence.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The movement relied on trained engineers and technical bodies for planning; inferred as a modernizing faith in technique.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power postdates the movement's founding era and no source touches energy technology, so this is left neutral.

revolution-justified.rationale: Venizelism arose from the Goudi military coup and the 1916 Thessaloniki rebellion, yet it sought constitutional order and fought communism.

experts-over-public.rationale: Technical organizations staffed by trained engineers led planning and the movement spoke of rule by merit; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: The state planned through technical bodies in a capitalist economy; Bolshevism was rejected.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred from the moderate capitalism and anti-Bolshevik stance.

land-value-tax.rationale: The sources on land policy describe expropriation and settlement of landless peasants, not a land-value tax, so no position is inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The 1911 constitution speaks of equal tax burdens but nothing in the sources addresses inheritance taxation.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: A strict protectionism was adopted to promote Greece's rudimentary industry.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Economic policy aimed to improve agriculture and industry through state technical organizations and planning.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Venizelists settled landless peasants and allowed expropriation to create small farmers, especially in Thessaly.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Rejected Bolshevism and advocated moderate capitalism.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The movement legalized labour organizations within a liberal framework rather than corporatist bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Liberal Party competed in parliamentary elections and Venizelism defined itself as liberal democracy against Bolshevik authoritarianism.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Venizelos preferred crowned democracy, yet most of his supporters favoured a republic; the movement was genuinely split.

democracy-best.rationale: Venizelism is called a liberal democracy movement, but the movement also backed military coups, so conviction is not total.

direct-votes.rationale: Representative parliamentary government is assumed; no direct democracy tradition documented.

right-to-secede.rationale: The movement was an irredentist nation-builder that sought to enlarge a unitary state.

natural-rulers.rationale: It stood for merit-based advancement of urban middle classes against a palace establishment.

political-violence-never.rationale: Venizelos led an armed rebellion in 1916 and the movement supported the 1909 and 1922 military movements.

war-builds-character.rationale: Venizelos treated war as an instrument of national aims, not as character-building.

separate-church-state.rationale: Secularist currents existed but Orthodoxy remained linked to the Greek nation and the 1911 constitution made no separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: A secularist liberal movement does not base law on scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: It built state institutions, judicial independence and rule of law.

military-superiority.rationale: It strengthened the army and navy to win national aims; superiority over rivals is inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The movement favoured one state for each predominantly single-ethnicity territory.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Venizelos argued socialism could be democratic while rejecting Bolshevik class-war politics.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Moderate capitalism and merit orientation do not aim at equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The question has no counterpart in Greek irredentist politics, so the movement is treated as having no view.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not applicable; the movement fought Ottoman and later British rule in Cyprus only through enosis aims.

civilizational-union.rationale: It aimed at union of Greek lands, not civilizational union.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Venizelism has no documented moral theory of self-interest; its liberalism is political and national, so this stays neutral.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The 1911 constitution strengthened individual rights, and nationalism asked duty in war; balanced.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy is anachronistic for this movement and none of the sources raise it.

limit-population.rationale: A movement concerned with national strength and settling refugees would not favour limiting population; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Transhumanist questions are far outside the movement's era and no source speaks to them.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement's technocratic bent toward engineers hints at mild distrust of replacing political judgment with algorithms, but this is only inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption is far outside the era and no position can be drawn from the sources.

restore-past-order.rationale: Venizelism opposed the conservative palace establishment and promoted modernization.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Venizelos is often described as pragmatic, but there is no stated doctrine.

direct-action.rationale: Elections were central to the Liberal Party, though coups also played a role.

means-match-ends.rationale: Neither source records a Venizelist view on prefigurative methods; it used coups and elections alike.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Inferred from capitalism and industrial development goals.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Moderate capitalism rejects need-based distribution; inferred.

profit-exploitation.rationale: It rejected Bolshevik analysis and favoured moderate capitalism.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Venizelos rejected Bolshevism and introduced the 1929 Idionymon.

collective-farming.rationale: Land policy gave plots to landless peasants rather than collectivizing.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Inferred from rejection of Marxism and its pro-Entente liberal framing.

taxation-theft.rationale: A state-building movement; the constitution prescribed equality in taxation.

harm-principle.rationale: Inferred from liberal rights tradition in the 1911 constitution.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Liberal on individual rights, yet nationalism treats the nation as a collective; no documented view.

conscription.rationale: Army reform under Venizelos built a modern conscript force, and war aims needed mobilization.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The movement built a parliamentary nation-state, and emigration as a check on government never appears in its sources; mildly opposed by inference.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred from technocratic planning rather than customer ideology.

positive-liberty.rationale: Free compulsory education and labour protections suggest that the state should supply conditions of freedom; inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: No source records Venizelist claims about universities or media power, so the answer is neutral.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Nationalism was ethnic-linguistic and civic-liberal, not explicitly biological; inferred.

organic-representation.rationale: Parliamentary liberal representation, not corporate bodies.

total-state.rationale: Liberal democracy opposed to authoritarian systems.

national-rebirth.rationale: The Megali Idea and modernization were framed as national regeneration; inferred from nationalism.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Venizelos pursued gains in Thrace and Western Anatolia under the Megali Idea.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: A modern state built on law, merit and constitutional government.

bound-labor.rationale: It settled landless peasants and promoted modernization.

universal-morality.rationale: Venizelism is a political movement without a stated moral epistemology, so no position can be drawn from the sources.

single-common-good.rationale: The movement had no stated theory of the common good; it combined liberal pluralism with a national goal, so this stays neutral.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Greek refugees from Turkey were settled in Greece and Venizelist sentiment welcomed co-ethnics; inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: The 1911 constitution made katharevousa official; revival of fallen language is not the issue.

school-vouchers.rationale: The state expanded compulsory free education; vouchers are anachronistic.

economic-freedom.rationale: Moderate capitalism and open markets with government approval imply support, though protectionist.

rule-by-example.rationale: Rule of law and constitutional modernization are the opposite.

national-self-determination.rationale: The movement favoured one state for each predominantly single-ethnicity territory and argued Greek claims from nationality at the Peace Conference.

force-without-un.rationale: The UN did not exist in the movement's lifetime and the question is anachronistic.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Secularist but not anti-religious; the nation remained Orthodox.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Social-insurance debates on citizens versus migrants are not recorded in the sources on Venizelism.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Workfare conditionality is not recorded in the sources; the 1910s Liberal social laws concerned labour protections instead.

class-collaboration.rationale: Moderate liberal-capitalist framing with legalized labour organizations over class war.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not a theme; the national cause values heritage.

dominated-front.rationale: Venizelism was pro-Western and allied with the Entente and later the Allies.

workers-nation.rationale: The Idionymon law and anti-Bolshevism favoured national over class organization, but no theory of this question exists.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The 1910-14 labour laws protected women workers with limits like night work, but no stated position.

ban-interest.rationale: A movement backing moderate capitalism and open markets would not outlaw lending at interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not part of the movement; inferred.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy production policy is anachronistic and absent from the sources.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Greece's immigration questions were mainly about co-ethnic refugees, so assimilation of foreign immigrants is not documented.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy theory not in the movement.

proportional-representation.rationale: No documented preference; the Liberals backed various electoral laws.

national-mission.rationale: Greece's liberal mission was tied to Megali Idea, but not spreading governmental form.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The sources show only labour protections for women workers, not any analysis of patriarchy; mildly negative by inference from its era.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Venizelism mobilized urban middle classes against the conservative palace-linked establishment; inferred.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not part of the program; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Transitional-justice accountability for past killings is not discussed in the sources on Venizelism.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Liberal governments built labour law, education and technical state agencies.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Venizelist nationalism was linguistic and civic-liberal, with no program against mixed marriage in any source.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The 1911 reforms strengthened rights and civic equality; the movement's liberalism suggests this, though nationalism complicates it.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Settler-colonial theory has no connection to the movement; neutral.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The unified modern nation-state implies uniform law; religion-based family law for minorities existed, so low.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A question tied to South Asian politics with no counterpart in Greek liberalism.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Orthodox religious education remained in Greek schools; secularism was limited.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Venizelos rejected Bolshevism and the Soviet theory of the state, so he would not endorse a strengthening socialist state.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Parliamentary liberal democracy, and the nationality principle that populations decide.

trade-surplus.rationale: Protectionist but no documented export-surplus doctrine.

population-transfer.rationale: Venizelos negotiated the Lausanne exchange as Greek delegate, and Venizelist refugees supported him.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Not a pacifist movement; led a war and a rebellion.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The sources do not give a Venizelist view of struggle as a driver of progress, so this stays neutral.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Venizelos introduced the Idionymon anticommunist law of 1929.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The republican-theory idea of freedom is not discussed in the sources, though 1911 rights protections lean liberal.

separated-powers.rationale: The 1911 revision strengthened judicial independence, an Electoral Court and the State Council.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Social democratic strand versus liberal strand; unresolved.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: British council housing is far outside the movement's context.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labour organizations were allowed, yet the Idionymon curbed subversive activity; split.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Malthusian explanations of poverty do not appear in the sources; Venizelist policy blamed land distribution and backwardness, so mildly disagree.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Venizelism's ethnic-nation stance suggests some agreement, but civic liberal nationalism tempers it.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Venizelist governments used emergency measures in war and the Thessaloniki period; split by era.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls in scarcity are not documented in the sources on Venizelism, so neutral.

party-controls-media.rationale: A liberal-democratic party could not support party control of the media.

party-commands-army.rationale: The 1916 and 1909 military roles aside, Venizelism rejects party armies.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization rules are not covered in the sources on Venizelism.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: No source records a Venizelist view on pay for legislators; the movement was a bourgeois-liberal party, so mild disagreement is inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The sources do not describe internal party discipline rules of the Liberal Party.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: A supranational union is anachronistic here; the movement sought national unification, not pooled sovereignty.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The crown prince/king and prime minister quarrelled over command; Venizelos preferred ministerial control during the schism, but not stated in sources.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The Orthodox Church was episcopal but no view is documented.

clerical-rule.rationale: Venizelism is described as secularist, so clerical political authority is rejected.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Venizelos fought for the Entente and national war aims; internationalist defeatism is the communist view he rejected.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: A liberal movement that strengthened individual freedoms would not endorse moral censorship, though no source states it.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits for presidents are not discussed in the sources; Venizelos was repeatedly prime minister under a parliamentary system.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The movement was defined by alliance with the Entente.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: An inference from its moderate capitalism that forced home ownership is not part of its program.

people-in-arms.rationale: Venizelos favoured a professional modernized army with foreign missions.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: It represented urban classes against a rural-conservative establishment.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reuniting Greek populations in separate territories was the Megali Idea.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: It was the party of urban educated classes.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Cultural relativism does not appear in the sources, and Hellenic nationalism leans toward valuing Greek civilization; left neutral.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from the era's norms; Venizelist governments executed leaders after 1922 but this is not documented in my sources.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Anachronistic for the era; the 1911 reform did make schooling compulsory, but no curriculum content on sex education is documented.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed in any source on the movement.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Ethnic-national citizenship is plausible for a Greek irredentist movement.

minority-language-support.rationale: One state per ethnic territory and the 1911 constitution made one language official.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and Venizelos's Cretan constitution avoided religious references so all would be represented.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Millian arguments about conformity are not recorded in the sources on Venizelism.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Greece was a debtor reliant on Entente loans but no repudiation stance is documented.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The movement pursued national unification and industrial protection, but no source ties independence to property restructuring.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The 1911 constitution was adopted by a Revisionary National Assembly under Venizelos.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Democracy-oriented; though some authoritarian episodes occurred.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Foreign aid duties are anachronistic for the era and absent from the sources.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons postdate the movement's main period.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central bank independence is an anachronistic question absent from the sources.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Irredentist territorial claims were central, though Venizelos accepted concessions such as the 1930 Ankara agreement.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The 1911 reform allowed expropriation for landless farmers while protecting property.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The sources only record Venizelos's rejection of Bolshevism, not an analysis of whether the USSR was state capitalist.

precautionary-principle.rationale: The precautionary principle is a late twentieth-century concept outside the movement's frame.

collective-defense.rationale: Venizelism was pro-Entente and pro-Western allied; collective security pacts were central.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Irredentism concerned Greek-inhabited lands; no stated view.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Secularist wing exists but no documented program.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Crowned democracy treats the monarch above party politics, and Venizelos protected the Crown's prerogatives.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not directly documented, but a unifying nationalist state-builder would be inclined to keep territory together.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not documented; the movement favored centralized nation-state building rather than special regional arrangements.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Liberal constitutionalism with monarch as constitutional.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The 1911 constitution mandated equality in tax burdens but no flat tax.

character-from-environment.rationale: The sources give no Venizelist view of nature versus nurture.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The 1911 revision aimed at the rule of law.

space-expansion.rationale: Space exploration is far outside the movement's era.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Crowned democracy mixes monarchy and parliament, but not stated as such.

leader-cult.rationale: Venizelos attracted a personal following; adherents were split.

equal-parenting.rationale: Shared-custody presumptions are anachronistic and absent from the sources.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Venizelos rejected Bolshevik socialism, so the question of class struggle within socialism is outside its frame, with mild disagreement.

land-redistribution.rationale: Venizelos settled landless peasants in Thessaly and the constitution allowed expropriation for landless farmers.

refugee-return.rationale: Venizelos agreed to the Lausanne exchange without return.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Venizelos's claims in Thrace and Western Anatolia rested on Greek populations living there.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Venizelism is described as secularist and the 1911 reforms strengthened individual freedoms, so punishing apostasy is rejected.

women-must-cover.rationale: A secularist, liberal movement would not legislate dress for women.

common-currency.rationale: A multinational currency is anachronistic and unmentioned in the sources.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The movement sought union of Greek-populated lands, not union with kin peoples sharing a language family.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not documented; ethnic-nation preference suggests limited autonomy.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The question concerns diaspora minorities in a persecution context and has no direct counterpart in the sources on Venizelism.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Venizelos separated democratic socialism from Marxism-Leninism, and the sources show no historical-materialist reading of events.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust is not discussed in the sources on Venizelist economic policy.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are not discussed in the sources.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Rule of law with independent courts.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas for public bodies are anachronistic; the era's women's role was limited to labour protections.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Linked trade standards are an anachronistic late-twentieth-century idea.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Goudi coup and 1916 movement were military, but these were not Marxist foco theory.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Merit orientation versus palace-linked elites; but monarchy retained by Venizelos.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The sources do not record a Venizelist theory of tutelage; its irredentism rested on nationality.

patriotic-education.rationale: Compulsory national education under liberal nationalism.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Affirmative action in admissions has no counterpart in the movement's context.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary-reform proposals do not appear in the sources, so mild disagreement is inferred from its moderate capitalism.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Greek aims were territorial union in former Ottoman areas, but the sources do not frame it as cultivating influence, so neutral.

delink-world-market.rationale: Protectionist but integrated into Western alliances.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Not documented; its civic liberalism with rights protections suggests mild disagreement.

elective-rulers.rationale: Venizelos favoured crowned democracy while his supporters preferred republic.

minority-veto.rationale: A parliamentary movement that governed by majority would not accept unanimity or minority vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Venizelos resisted King Constantine in 1916 over constitutional conflict.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Venizelism was an activist modernizing movement, so withdrawal is opposed.

paid-care-work.rationale: Wages for domestic work are anachronistic and absent from the sources.

office-by-exam.rationale: The 1911 constitution guaranteed civil-service tenure and merit orientation.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The movement favored open markets with government approval, but sources record no stance on foreign buyers of strategic firms.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not covered in the sources, so mild disagreement is inferred from conventional values of an Orthodox liberal party.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The movement worked through ordinary parliamentary representation, not mandated delegates.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Private pension accounts are anachronistic and absent from the sources.

single-official-language.rationale: The 1911 constitution declared katharevousa the official language.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land ownership by foreigners is not covered in the sources.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: A modern American legal doctrine with no counterpart in the sources.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Consumer culture critique is not documented in the sources.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Sources do not describe Venizelist doctrine on arming insurgents, though Greek irredentism did use irregulars elsewhere.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Bloc intervention is a Cold War idea with no counterpart in the sources.

corporate-influence.rationale: Lobbying and campaign finance are not discussed in the sources.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Foreign funding of NGOs is not discussed in the sources.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Family subsidies for births are not documented in the sources.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local property restrictions are not discussed in the sources.

job-guarantee.rationale: A state employer of last resort goes beyond the moderate capitalism the sources attribute to Venizelism.

democratic-peace.rationale: Democratic-peace theory is not discussed in the sources, though the movement's liberal pro-Western alignment is compatible with it.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The movement built rule of law and a modern state, which presumes a duty to obey.

non-intervention.rationale: Venizelos depended on great-power intervention and Allied backing.

industrial-unions.rationale: The organizational form of unions is not discussed in the sources.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy theories about a minority are not part of the movement's program.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: An inference from conventional Orthodox social values; the sources do not address marriage law.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Freedom-of-information rights are not discussed in the sources.

informal-organisation.rationale: The Liberal Party was a conventional parliamentary party, not an informal-affinity-group movement.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Not documented; Venizelos accepted Treaty obligations such as Lausanne and Allied arbitration.

religious-nation.rationale: Civic-liberal nationalism and secularist currents, though Orthodoxy and Hellenism overlapped.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Venizelos seeking recognition of Greece as an equal at the peace conference rather than ritual submission, while still relying on Allied backing.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Venizelos building a centralised modernising state that settled Thessaly and integrated new lands under one treasury.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Not addressed; the Liberal programme sought moderate capitalism with land reform and not common ownership of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Venizelism opposed Bolshevism, including the Idionymon law against subversive ideas; the answer for coexistence versus defeat is inferred.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the liberal mixed-economy approach with state modernisation and private enterprise.

religion-illusion.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a liberal-nationalist current that kept the Orthodox Church as a national institution.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Venizelism combining moderate capitalism with protection and modernisation as the road to national strength.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Venizelist labour laws were limited social legislation; inferred that it did not tie women equality to transforming the economy.

socialized-care.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a liberal reform programme that left domestic work to families.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal modernisers backing language reform toward the demotic, not a purge of loanwords.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not addressed; the 1911 constitution protected rights, but Venizelos also revised the settlement with the Ottomans and minorities by treaty exchange.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a state-building and market-oriented programme that did not seek small communal societies.

majority-settlement.rationale: Venizelos settled Greek populations in newly won lands such as Thessaly and Macedonia; an inference that settlement was an accepted way to bind territory to Greece.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Venizelism accepting moderate capitalism while opposing Bolshevism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The Megali Idea held that Greek-populated lands, grounded in historic and ethnic ties, should be united with Greece, and Venizelos pressed this case at Paris.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not an issue of the era; a liberal-nationalist current would reject denial of a documented genocide, inferred from its liberal rule-of-law principles.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed; a liberal rule-of-law modernizing movement is inferred to lean against criminalizing private conduct, though era norms were conservative.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Venizelism stood for parliamentary rule of law and the 1911 rights charter, though the 1929 Idionymon targeted communist agitation specifically rather than all opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The 1911 constitution kept Orthodoxy as the prevailing religion but guaranteed freedom of worship; inferred that adherents would not punish open practice of other faiths.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Greece had no overseas colonies and Venizelism sought union of Greek lands rather than colonial exploitation; inferred from its liberal-nationalist principles.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not part of a Greek Orthodox liberal-nationalist outlook; inferred rejection of a Muslim religious-duty doctrine.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Venizelists did fight the crown, but on constitutional and national grounds, not religious law; inferred rejection of a religious-law test of legitimacy.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Venizelism favoured representative parliamentary government run by a modernizing state, not direct participation; inferred from its program.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Class and gender oppression were outside the program; the movement was a cross-class liberal coalition, so adherents would not endorse the framework.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic for 1910-36; inferred reluctance from the era's liberal-conservative social norms.

assisted-dying.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred opposition from the Orthodox-majority setting of the movement.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Venizelism defined itself as a liberal pole against both the royalist right and Bolshevism, so it kept the division rather than dissolving it.

alienated-labor.rationale: The movement favoured moderate capitalism with some labour legislation and rejected Marxism; alienation is a Marxist concept it did not adopt.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not an issue in its time; the 1930 rapprochement with Turkey and the liberal outlook point against civilizational incompatibility claims.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Venizelism rested on constitutional, national sovereignty and not divine right; inferred from the 1911 constitutional revision.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Adherents are likely split: a modernizing secular-leaning state coexisted with a prevailing Orthodox church; the issue was not raised.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the program bears on it.

social-market-economy.rationale: Its mix of market capitalism, protectionism and social legislation resembles a regulated mixed economy, inferred from the economic stance.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Venizelos rebuilt the army and navy with foreign missions and fought several wars, so abolition is contrary to the program.

rich-first.rationale: Not addressed; protectionist state-led development is neither an endorsement of unequal growth nor a rejection of it.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Venizelism was defined by pro-Entente and pro-Western alignment, bringing Greece into the Allied camp in 1917.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Venizelism kept the crowned democracy and the Glucksburg dynasty under the 1911 constitution, so hereditary succession of the head of state was accepted, though the leader of a state here is read broadly.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Venizelist liberal capitalism relied on the National Bank and private finance; user-owned at-cost credit was not on its agenda, inferred from its moderate-capitalist stance.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Venizelos courted Western creditors and Entente backing and pursued fiscal orthodoxy; refusing lender conditions is inferred as contrary to its pro-Western alignment.

property-franchise.rationale: Venizelism extended liberal, constitutional government and the 1911 revision kept universal male suffrage, so a property qualification was not its position.

domination-women-nature.rationale: An ecofeminist claim foreign to a liberal-nationalist modernizing movement; inferred from its state-modernization focus and its limited women's-rights agenda.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept; Venizelism opposed Bolshevism and accepted moderate capitalism, so adherents would reject the claim, inferred from that anti-Marxism.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Venizelism was a bourgeois-liberal movement that defended formal liberties; it would not have accepted that they are hollow under wealthy ownership, inferred from its liberal outlook.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule of law and constitutional government under the 1911 revision, including judicial independence, were core Venizelist reforms.

racial-franchise.rationale: Venizelism was irredentist but civic in constitution, and Venizelos protected minority rights and gave them votes in the new lands, so a racial franchise was not its position.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in Venizelism bears on the internet, and adherents' liberal reformism neither clearly favours nor opposes it.

open-government-data.rationale: Anachronistic; Venizelist liberalism favoured accountable, modern administration, but publishing records was not an issue in the period.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Venizelos introduced civil-law modernization, but marriage remained religious in the period; inferred opposition from its liberal secularizing reforms.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Venizelos sought to integrate minorities in the enlarged state and negotiated their protection at Paris, so boycotts of minority shops ran against his policy.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Anachronistic; Venizelism relied on parliaments and the constituent National Assembly, inferred as preferring representative institutions to sortition.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Venizelism clashed with the palace and clergy over some reforms but kept Orthodoxy as the state religion; adherents were split, inferred.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Venizelist governments pursued land settlement and expropriation for landless farmers under the 1911 constitution, suggesting concern about concentrated holdings, though the movement was pro-capitalist.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed in 1910-1936; inferred from the conservative social norms of the period and a liberal nationalism focused on state and nation.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Venizelism was Orthodox-respecting liberal nationalism; promoting atheism through schools is inferred to be far outside it.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Venizelism stressed rule of law and a modernized state apparatus, so abolishing police and prisons is incompatible with it.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: A unitary nation-state governed by parliamentary majorities is inferred; the movement never proposed communal executive power-sharing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Venizelist social legislation and state modernization imply a role for government in helping the poor; inferred from the moderate mixed-economy stance.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a liberal parliamentary tradition built around long-serving statesmen such as Venizelos himself.

vote-delegation.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a representative parliamentary model with no hint of direct or delegated voting.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic for the period; inferred that adherents would be indifferent, since the movement's concerns were national and constitutional.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the Orthodox Church context of 1910-1936 Greece, where women held no clerical office and the movement did not challenge this.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from the period's Greek family norms; Venizelism did not push family-law equality, though liberal reform leanings soften the answer.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The liberal-nationalist state of the era tied political rights to citizenship, so rights for foreign residents are inferred to be rejected.

rent-control.rationale: The labour laws of 1910-14 did not cover rents, and adherents ranged from liberal to social democratic.

abolish-ip.rationale: Intellectual property was not an issue of the era and a liberal-capitalist movement would be expected to uphold it, inferred.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Venizelos modernised the army with foreign missions, but liberal Venizelism had no drilled youth movement, so this is inferred as disagreement.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear weapons are anachronistic for the movement, and no direction can be inferred.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Venizelos relied on the Entente alliance and Allied authority at Smyrna, so hosting allied forces is inferred as acceptable.

recognise-genocide.rationale: A liberal nationalist movement concerned with persecuted Greeks would be expected to favour recognition of mass killings, inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Venizelism was a mixed economy ranging from liberal to social democratic, with no stated line on income from property.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The movement conducted wars and the Smyrna landing, so a ban on killing in defence is inferred to be rejected.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Megali Idea drew on a Greek continuity from antiquity and Byzantium, from which agreement is inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: A liberal-nationalist movement of 1910-36 is inferred to treat sex as natural.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: A liberal-nationalist movement of 1910-36 is inferred to treat women as a single category in law.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Venizelism was liberal and secular in outlook, so honour for the war dead is likely but sainthood is not stated.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Venizelism was liberal and state-modernising and did not frame politics as a spiritual war, inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The Megali Idea aimed to unite Greek-populated lands with the Greek state, which is the opposite of a homeland serving a diaspora.

culture-before-state.rationale: Venizelos put state modernisation and the rule of law first in 1910-14, so culture before state is rejected.

god-not-male.rationale: The movement stated no religious position on this.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: The movement stated no religious position on this.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The 1911 constitution and Venizelos's minority treaties leave economic life open to citizens of all communities, inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The Megali Idea and the Paris Peace Conference claims sought to unite Greek-populated regions into one state.

independent-unions.rationale: A liberal-modernizing movement would accept independent unions; inferred, not a Venizelist program item.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Venizelism was liberal and moderately capitalist and opposed Bolshevism, so it did not make workers' power the test of socialism; inferred.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Mixed-economy liberals were split on public versus private local services.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from the liberal constitutional tradition; second chambers were debated in Greek constitutional revisions.

municipal-property.rationale: The movement backed moderate capitalism and a national state, not community ownership of production.

confederal-coordination.rationale: A centralizing modernizing state, not confederal local assemblies, was the Venizelist aim.

family-wage.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; adherents are split.

anonymous-payments.rationale: A rule-of-law state builder would back state oversight of payments; inferred.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred from the movement's liberal commitment to rule of law and individual rights.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The movement was Orthodox-Christian in culture but took no stated position on this.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Greece was a unitary state, so inferred that the national parliament held final authority over local government.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The Megali Idea was national and cultural, not racial in an organising sense; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Venizelist national pride was about the Greek nation, and the statement is about race.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The Megali Idea pursued Greek territorial claims by war and at the Paris Peace Conference, so the movement did not limit force to self-defence.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The Megali Idea claimed Greek-speaking lands across Thrace and Anatolia as one nation, but Greek identity also rested on Orthodoxy, so language alone is not the whole test.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from the liberal rule-of-law state of the 1911 constitution, which treated citizens individually; not a documented Venizelist position.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Venizelism was pro-Entente and saw great powers as patrons, though it feared their veto of Greek claims; no stated position, inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from the Liberal Party's state modernization and education reform program of 1910-14; free tuition itself is not documented.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Anachronistic for 1910-1936; no stated position and nothing in the program to infer from.

future-generations.rationale: Anachronistic; mild agreement inferred from the liberal-modernizing stress on building up the state for later generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Women's suffrage was resisted by the Liberals before 1930 and no distinct-values claim was made; inferred as neutral.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from the army build-up for the Balkan Wars and the irredentist program, which needed strong forces.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Venizelos appealed to Wilsonian open diplomacy at Paris while relying on the secret-treaty practices of the era; split, inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from the moderate capitalism with protectionism the Liberals practised, which favoured state steering of the economy.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Venizelos's rule-of-law and state-building reforms imply a monopoly of force by state forces, inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Venizelism pursued the Megali Idea through war and relied on a modernized army and navy, so refusing to fight is rejected.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The 1910-14 labour laws regulated unions and conditions but adherents ranged from liberals to social democrats; inferred.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: No tax credit system existed and the programme was a moderate capitalism with limited social legislation; inferred.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses legal borrowing limits; the era's governments borrowed for war and modernization.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Venizelism pursued Greek claims within the existing Entente order, not a restructuring of the economy in favour of poorer states; inferred.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Venizelism reformed and modernized the state through constitutional revision rather than destroying it, and opposed Bolshevism.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The programme was a moderate capitalism with protectionism and technical planning, not open experimentation; inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Anachronistic; a liberal-modernizing state of the period is inferred not to price ecosystems.

sacred-nation.rationale: The Megali Idea made the Greek nation, to be united across its lands, a central object of devotion, though not framed in sacred terms.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Anachronistic; no student loan system existed and the programme had no such aim.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Venizelism centralized the state and pursued national unity, so regional exploitation claims are inferred to be rejected.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Liberal rights in the 1911 constitution imply a shared basis of dignity; inferred.

public-service-media.rationale: Era predates public broadcasting; adherents' views on state-funded media cannot be read from the sources.

missingStatements.text: Greek-speaking populations should be reunited with the Greek state through the peace settlement after a war.
missingStatements.rationale: Venizelos claimed Thrace and Western Anatolia at the Peace Conference on grounds of Greek population, the core of the Megali Idea.

notes: The strand is internally split on monarchy (Venizelos moderate, most supporters republican) and economics (liberal to social democratic). Several answers rest on the thin English-language sources available and the open-access Wikipedia coverage carries a needs-citations banner; no scholarly monograph was opened.
